judgements.justification: A's Reviewer_yauQ wrongly said SQIL was the only imitation baseline and Reviewer_3uQ8 wrongly read sawyer_push as underspecified, but the rebuttal corrected both and the final 7s rest on correct points (C-learning overlap, simple image tasks).
B's chair gave an oral on 8, 9, 7, 8 (mean 8.0) and restated the scores; the tier did not exceed what the ratings supported.
B's Reviewer_xycR gave the only 9 of seven reviews on one paragraph of praise ('the work is solid') and one minor comment, which lifted B's mean.
No flaw was disclosed on one forum only; the C-learning concession answered A's own reviewer.
A weighed the conceded C-learning overlap; B never learned of it, so neither committee ignored a known flaw.
The rebuttal raised scores in both committees (Reviewer_yauQ in A; Reviewer_LgSM and Reviewer_9r4w in B).
Only A raised the correct, conceded point that the theory follows the authors' C-learning analysis, and the simple image tasks that the paper concedes.
The shared points (some prior-work overlap, experimental depth) were not treated as tier-setting by either side; the gap comes from different issues and score calibration.
Neither chair resolved a split by adopting one reviewer's position; both followed unsplit reviews.
B's Reviewer_LgSM raised to 8 'after reading the other reviews and the authors' responses to them', with no new evidence; the reply to LgSM was only a promise.
No reviewer's question was misread or left unanswered in a way that held a score down.
B's Reviewer_xycR's 9 rested on assertion, with no engagement after the rebuttal, and counted unchallenged in a two-sentence meta-review.
A's chair gave a poster consistent with 7, 7, 8; no rejection against a majority.
Neither chair decided by a borderline mean against a stated own view.
No below-threshold score is involved.
Both committees read the paper as the same kind of methodological RL contribution.
No reviewer said the technical core was outside their expertise.
No committee required something extra of this kind of paper.
B's checkable claims behind its praise were all correct.
No below-threshold score was kept after its main concern was answered.
Neither committee was asked to credit or refuse promised revisions in a way that set the tier.
No reviewer's stated stance diverged from an unedited score.
No off-record extra reviewer.
No clarity verdict split by reviewer distance from the field.
Reviewer_LgSM raised silently, but the review text did not argue against acceptance.
No silent detractor was set aside.
B's 9 came from a thin review, not a detailed checked reading, and A also had an 8.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading.
No reviewer contested the premise from another tradition.
B's meta-review is two sentences ('well-received ... discussion strengthened the acceptance score') and gives no reason for the oral tier.
Only A's Reviewer_yauQ knew the closely related C-learning work, checked the theory's novelty against it and asked for that baseline; B's reviewers took the comparisons as 'comprehensive'.
A's chair overstated initial agreement on novelty, but in the favourable direction, not toward its lower tier; B's summary matches its record.
A's chair limited the 'rather significant impact' to 'some domains', a breadth limit that fits its poster; B raised no breadth concern.
A had no low-scoring misreading detractor; its lowest ratings were 7.
Only A, in answer to Reviewer_yauQ, got a new C-learning-variant result (about 0.07 against 0.2 return), and yauQ raised; B never saw it.
B's high scores do not come from low-confidence reviews outweighing an expert; all A confidences are 4.
No late post-response objection.
B's careful reviews are no more favourable than A's (B's Reviewer_6QWr wrote 'very high quality' and gave 7), yet B's ratings run higher, partly from a 9 on generic praise.
No committee judged a headline claim overstated.

reasoning: Both committees judged the paper a clear accept, and their careful reviews are close (7, 7 in A; 7, 8 in B). B's oral rests on higher scores from a thin, unengaged 9 (R03, R12), a reason-free raise after reading other reviews (R10), more lenient scoring for similar praise (R38), and a two-sentence meta-review that gives no case for the oral (R30). A heard the conceded C-learning overlap that B did not (R07, R31), got a new result in answer (R35), and its chair limited impact to some domains (R33). Every stage 1 candidate maps to an existing reason, so no reason is added.
